newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn issues 5 bln dmk of 10-yr, 6 pct Bund.
newsitem.headline: Bonn issues 5 bln dmk of 10-yr, 6 pct Bund.

text.p: The German government on Tuesday issued five billion marks of a new 10-year, six percent coupon bond to the Federal Bond Consortium, the Bundesbank as issuing agent said on Tuesday.
The bond was priced at 101.05 and the yield is 5.86 percent. A second tranche of the bond will be issued in an auction with bids due by 1000 GMT on Wednesday.
Traders had expected a coupon of around six percent or possibly 5 7/8 percent.
Bonn issues 5 bln dmk of 10-yr, 6 pct Bund
The bond matures on January 4, 2007 with the first interest payment due on January 4, 1998.
The Bundesbank has said that up to 15 billion marks of 10-year paper will be issued this week, followed by a further 10 billion marks worth in the third 10 days of January.

The bond, the first federal 10-year bond issue since last April, will be listed on Monday, January 13 and is expected to be strippable from July 1997 onwards. Stripping refers to allowing separate trading of a bond's principal and coupon.
In Germany the Federal Bond Consortium arranges details of a new bond issue with the Bundesbank and receives a first tranche, with a second portion issued in an auction one day later.
The Bundesbank retains a third portion of the issue for market-tending purposes.
